sentences.text: COMMONJUDGMENT

The petitioner in M.V.C. No.359/2021 filed claim petition under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner in M.V.C.No.360/2021 filed claim petition under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking compensation for the death of one Sri.Shivaraju caused in a road traffic accident.
3. These two petitions have arisen out of same accident.
Petitioners and respondents are one and the same.
Therefore as per order on I.A.No.I, these two petitions have been clubbed together for common evidence and common disposal.
The case of the petitioners is as follows:

That on 30.10.2020 at about 9.45 a.m., deceased Shivaraju in M.V.C. No.360/2021 was riding Bajaj Discover Motor Cycle bearing No.KA44Q9026 along with his father by name Veerabhadraiah who is the petitioner in MVC No.359/2021 on TuruvekereYediyur road, while so proceeding reached near Mukkundas Lane, Garudanahalli village, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala, Mandya, at that time the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA447686 came from opposite direction i.e., from Yediyur side drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motorcycle,
as a result petitioner in MVC 359/2021 has sustained Nalinakshi vs Ramesh B.M on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68281510/
3 injuries and one Shivaraju was succumbed to the fatal injuries and died on the spot.

5. Immediately after the accident petitioner in MVC No.
359/2021 was taken to Turuvekere Government Hospital wherein he took first aid treatment and further shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital wherein he took treatment as inpatient.
He spent Rs.2, 00,000/ towards medical expenses, for conveyance, nourishment food and attendant charges.
He was aged 58 years, was working as Agriculturist and earning Rs.15, 000/ per month.
Due to permanent  SCCH24 6 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w  360/2021 disability suffered on account of grievous injuries he is not in a position to do the work.
He has suffered mental pain and agony, discomfort and other pecuniary and non pecuniary damages.
6. Immediately after the accident deceased Shivaraju in MVC No.360/2021 was taken to Adichunchanagiri Hospital wherein after postmortem examination the body was handed over to the petitioners.
They spent more than Rs.1, 00,000/ towards funeral and obsequious ceremony etc.
At the time of accident, deceased Shivaraju was hale and healthy and was doing Hotel Business, thereby earning a sum of Rs.25, 000/ per month.

Due to the sudden death ,
petitioners have suffered pain and mental agony and other pecuniary and nonpecuniary damages.
7. In pursuance to the notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels.

But the respondent No.1 has failed to file written statement,
hence taken as not filed.
 8. Respondent No.2 - ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company /insurer of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA 447686 in both the cases filed written statement denying the petition averments.
It is admitted by the respondent  SCCH24 7 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w  360/2021 No.1 that Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA447686 was insured with respondent No.2 at the time of alleged accident.

It is contended by the respondent no.2 that the driver of alleged offending vehicle had driven the vehicle without valid driving licence and also that offending vehicle had no valid permit and FC as on the date of accident and thereby violated the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, hence no liability can be attached to the respondent No.2.

It is further contended that Nalinakshi vs Ramesh B.M on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68281510/
4 the owner of alleged insured vehicle and the police have not intimated about the accident which is mandatory under Sec.134(c) and Sec.158 (6) of MV Act.

It is further submitted that there was no rash and negligent driving by its driver and that deceased was driving an uninsured vehicle,
without wearing the helmet and without observing traffic rules, hence deceased Mr.Shivaraju himself was the main architect for the unfortunate accident.
It has denied the involvement of offending vehicle and the manner of accident.
Contending thus the respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition.

9. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed in M.V.C.No 359/2021.

Issue No.1 and 2 in M.V.C.NO.359/2021 and M.V.C.No.360/2021:
As these issues are interconnected they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts.
P.W.1 Veerabhadraiah is the petitioner in MVC 359/2021 and P.W.2 - Nalinakshi is the wife of deceased in MVC No.360/2021.

P.W.1 and Pw2 have given evidence to the effect that at the time of accident the deceased Shivaraju was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA44Q9026 and Nalinakshi vs Ramesh B.M on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68281510/

6 P.W.1 was pillion rider, at that time, the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA447686 driving his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the motorcycle ridden by deceased Shivaraju and caused the accident, result of which PW.1/petitioner in MVC 359/2021 sustained grievous injuries and Shivaraju was died on the spot.

The respondents no 1 and 2 have seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners and submitted that rash and negligent riding of the two wheeler by the deceased is the sole cause for the accident and that deceased was not wearing helmet hence only he has sustained severe head injury and that at the time of accident the two wheeler had no valid insurance policy, hence submitted to dismiss the petition.
 17.

If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 22 feet,
and the spot of accident is at a distance of nearly 6 feet from the left edge of the tar road leads from Turuvekere to Yediyur.
Admittedly offending vehicle was coming from Yediyur towards Turuvekere.
The deceased and PW.1 were proceeding towards Yediyur in their two wheeler.

It means,
the deceased was proceeding on the left side of Turuvekere Yediyur road where as the driver of offending vehicle by encroaching nearly 16 feet road drove his vehicle on the extreme left side of Yediyur road and hit against to the two wheeler result of which this mishap has occurred.
Had the driver of the offending vehicle drive his vehicle on the left side of his road this accident would not have occurred.
SCCH24 12 MVC Nos.359/2021
Though the respondent no.2 has contended that at the time of accident deceased was not wearing helmet but there is no material to substantiate the said contention.

So far as not having insurance policy in respect of the two wheeler is concerned, if the charge sheet is perused, alleging that deceased who was the owner of the two wheeler ridden his vehicle without having valid insurance policy, he has been prosecuted for the offense punishable u/Sec.146 and 196 of IMV Act and filed abated charge sheet against him.

Though the PW.1 and 2 have deposed that at the time of accident the vehicle of the deceased was validly insured but no insurance policy which was in force as on the date of accident is produced before the court.

But the mere fact that the policy was not in force in respect of the two wheeler on Nalinakshi vs Ramesh B.M on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68281510/
7 that ground alone negligence cannot be attributed against the deceased unless the rash and negligent act contributed by the deceased is proved.

20. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.359/2021: P.W.1 has given evidence to the effect of his sustaining severe injuries.
Petitioner has produced abundant medical documents.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P.6 and examined the medical record officer at Adichunchanagiri hospital as PW.4.

On going through the medical documents it reveals that soon after the accident petitioner was taken to Turuvekere Government Hospital, thereafter taken to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, B.G. Nagara, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya and admitted as inpatient from 30.10.2020 to 23.11.2020.
He underwent surgery for ORIF with plates and screws for the right proximal tibia and ORIF with tension band wiring for the right patella was done on 11.11.2020.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained 4 injuries of which one is grievous in nature.
21. Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center is examined as Pw3 and produced recent Xray film and clinical report at Ex.P.24
and 25.

SCCH24 14 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w  360/2021 P.W.3 has deposed that petitioner has sustained right knee proximal tibia fracture with fracture of the right patella and he was treated at Adichunchanagiri Hospital with ORIF with plates and screws for the right proximal tibia and ORIF with tension band wiring for the right patella done on 11.11.2020.
Pw.3 further deposed that he examined petitioner clinically, radiologically and assessed the disability .

He further deposed that the petitioner has 46%

Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
22. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury and three simple injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/ towards pain and suffering.
SCCH24 15 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w
So far as medical expenses incurred by the petitioner , he has produced Ex.P10 62 medical bills for Rs.62,942/.

As such the petitioner is entitled for Rs.
62,942/ under the head medical expenses.
 24.
It is stated that petitioner was 58 years and working as Agriculturist, earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ p.m.
In this regard, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Hence notional income needs to be considered.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.14,500/ p.m.
 25.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment for 24 days as inpatient in Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Mandya.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature, it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.14,500/ p.m.
 SCCH24 16 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w  360/2021 for three months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.43,500/ towards loss of income during the laid down period .

From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment for several times.
Further for 24 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.35,000/
taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2020.

27. P.W.3 has deposed that petitioner has 46%
permanent disability in his right lower limb and 15% on whole body.
But Pw3 is not a treated doctor.

It is admitted by PW3 that he has assessed the disability without going through the follow up treatment records and that he has not taken the opinion from the treated doctor and that fractures of the PW.1 are united and that since PW.1 is aged nearly about 60 years he may have aged related problems and that one cannot bifurcate the age related problems with the  SCCH24 17 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w  360/2021 disability arisen out of the accidental injury.
By considering evidence of the PW.3 the court cannot blindly accept the percentage of disability assessed by the Pw3.
Hence this court inclines to take the disability to the extent of 10% on whole body instead of 16%.
28. The petitioner has contended that he is aged about 58 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P8 and Ex.P9 Aadhar card & PAN card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 01.06.1962, that means he was aged 58 years.
Hence considering the Aadhar card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 58 years.

29 . So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.14,500/ p.m , if 10% of loss of earning capacity is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 58 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 is '9'.
So by applying the multiplier '9' the future loss of income due to disability comes to 1,56,600/ (i.e., 14,500 x 10% x 9 x12 ).

Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for  SCCH24 18 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w Nalinakshi vs Ramesh B.M on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68281510/
10  360/2021 Rs.1,56,600/ towards future loss of income due to disability.

P.W.3 has stated that petitioner has to undergo another surgery for implant removal the cost of which will be Rs.60,000/.
But there is no estimation bill produced by the Petitioner or PW.3.
As borne out by records, the petitioner has taken treatment for 24 days and he has incurred medical expenses to the tune of Rs.62,9942/
Hence, it is unacceptable to say that for removal of implants it may cost Rs. 60,000/.

Therefore, looking in to the earlier treatment,
cost and nature of injuries and cross examination of PW.3, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.25,000/
is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.25,000/ under the head future medical expenses.

sentences.text: 11 petitioners contended that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Shivaraju.
The 1st petitioner is the wife, 2nd and 3rd petitioners are the minor daughters ad 4 th and 5th petitioners are the parents of the deceased, and hence they are entitled for compensation.
To prove the said fact they have produced aadhaar card of the petitioners and deceased, PAN cards of the petitioner no.1,4 and 5 and deceased, Family ration card etc .

33. Issue no 3 :
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned respective counsels, it can be said that the deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
As per Aadhaar card and PAN card of the deceased, the year of birth of the deceased was 1987.
Hence it can be gathered that as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 33 years.

34 . So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of the petitioners,
deceased was doing Hotel Business, thereby earning Rs.25,
000/ p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2020, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.14,500/ per month.

Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.14,500/ p.m.
 SCCH24 21 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w  360/2021  35.
This petition is being filed by the wife, minor daughters and parents of the deceased and they are the dependents of the deceased.

36. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife and married, 1/4th of the annual income is to be deducted Nalinakshi vs Ramesh B.M on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68281510/
12 towards the personal expenses and remaining 3/4th is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

37. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors /
Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to the actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
 SCCH24 22 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w  360/2021 of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25%
where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case as the deceased was 33 years, 40% should be added towards future prospects.
38. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.14,500/ if 40% is added towards the future prospect it comes around Rs.20,300/.
Out of it if 1/4th is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.15,225/ .
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 31 to 35 is 16.
Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.29,23,200/ (15,225/ x 16 x 12= 29,23,200/).

39. Because of the untimely death of deceased,
petitioner no.1 lost her husband, petitioner no.2 and 3 lost their father and petitioner no.4 and 5 have lost their son.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the  SCCH24 23 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w  360/2021 head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of Nalinakshi vs Ramesh B.M on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68281510/
13 consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/,
Rs.40,000/ and Rs.15,000/ respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

40. As per the ratio laid down by the hon'ble Apex court in Civil Appeal No 24102412/2013 in the case of Sri Ram General Insurance Company Ltd / Bhagat Singh Rawat and Others decided on 2 nd February 2023, it is held that "the notice in terms of the order dated 13/10/2020 was confined only to the aspects i.e the sum for loss of love and affection being Rs 50,000 and loss of consortium could not have been granted to each of the three dependents separately but in toto and that would be the amount quantified.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs  SCCH24 24 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w  360/2021 44,000/ in toto to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled to funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.16,500/ and Rs.16,500/
towards loss of estate.

41 . In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
 1 Loss of Estate Rs.16,500/
 2 Transportation and funeral  expenses Rs.16,500/
 3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs. 44,000/
 filial consortium and parental  consortium  4 Loss of Dependency Rs.29,23,200/
 Total Rs.30,00,200/

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.30,00,200/
(Rupees Thirty Lakhs Two Hundred only) and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
42. Admittedly as on the date of accident the policy in respect of offending vehicles was in force.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondents no 1 and 2 have seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners and submitted that rash and negligent riding of the two wheeler by the deceased is the sole cause for the accident and that deceased was not wearing helmet hence only he has sustained severe head injury and that at the time of accident the two wheeler had no valid insurance policy, hence submitted to dismiss the petition.
 17.
Had the driver of the offending vehicle drive his vehicle on the left side of his road this accident would not have occurred.
So far as not having insurance policy in respect of the two wheeler is concerned, if the charge sheet is perused, alleging that deceased who was the owner of the two wheeler ridden his vehicle without having valid insurance policy, he has been prosecuted for the offense punishable u/Sec.146 and 196 of IMV Act and filed abated charge sheet against him.
But the mere fact that the policy was not in force in respect of the two wheeler on Nalinakshi vs Ramesh B.M on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68281510/
7 that ground alone negligence cannot be attributed against the deceased unless the rash and negligent act contributed by the deceased is proved.
For not having valid insurance policy, the investigation officer rightly had filed abated charge sheet against the deceased for the offense u/Sec.
146 and 196 of IMV Act.
 19.
Hence, by relying upon the materials placed on record it can be said without any hesitation that the driver  SCCH24 13 MVC Nos.359/2021  C/w  360/2021 of the offending vehicle has solely contributed negligence.
Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
22. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury and three simple injuries.
Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/ towards pain and suffering.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment for 24 days as inpatient in Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Mandya.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature, it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period.
Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.14,500/ p.m.

So by applying the multiplier '9' the future loss of income due to disability comes to 1,56,600/ (i.e., 14,500 x 10% x 9 x12 ).

Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2020, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.14,500/ per month.
Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.14,500/ p.m.
